author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read Bitwarden organization event logs from the Public API (Teams and Enterprise). The example bridge in bridges/bitwarden-events pulls the events and posts them to HTTP Ingest. Sign-ins, wrong master passwords and wrong two-step login codes go to Auth, and every other event goes to CloudAudit.
notes:
Setup:
- Bitwarden offers organization event logs to other tools only through the Public API (Teams and Enterprise), so these parsers read events pulled by the example bridge in bridges/bitwarden-events and posted to HTTP Ingest.
- The bridge puts "bitwarden_record": "event" first and adds organizationId, and the email and name of the acting user and of the member from the member list, since an event names them only by ID.
- MSPs run one bridge per client organization.

Field mapping:
- Sign-ins (User_LoggedIn), wrong master passwords (User_FailedLogIn), wrong two-step login codes (User_FailedLogIn2fa) and first SSO sign-ins go to Auth, with the Bitwarden app as the logon application.
- Every other event goes to CloudAudit with the event name as the event name, its category (item, collection, group, member, organization, policy, secret, send and others) as the event type, and every ID it carries as a resource.
- Item, secret and Send events and vault exports are data events, and views, copies, autofills, retrievals and exports are read-only.
- Event and device names are the enum names in Bitwarden's Public API OpenAPI document; a newer code keeps the name event_<code>.

Time:
- Most events come from Bitwarden's apps, which send them about every 60 seconds with the device's time.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples follow the EventResponseModel in Bitwarden's OpenAPI document with made-up values, tagged by the bridge's own code.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (162 of 162 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs), and the parent's confirm string picked the same records there.
- Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent (162 of 162 fields, each line taken in 5 of 5 runs).
- No built-in parser claimed these records.

Known gaps:
- Bitwarden notes a modified client could suppress events.
